supported_claim: All ten methods improve substantially as target labels increase from 0.1% to 20% on the frozen Target12 panel.
evidence: Five-fold mean trajectories in the left and centre displays.
not_supported: The panel does not establish a universal learning law outside Target12.
positive_interpretation: Low-label calibration is measurable across predictor families.
negative_interpretation: A method-specific non-monotonic segment should be reported rather than smoothed away.

supported_claim: The fraction of full-label performance recovered is method dependent.
evidence: Right halves of split glyphs and descriptive relative log-AULC.
not_supported: Relative log-AULC is not an inferential ranking and does not make ten methods biological replicates.
positive_interpretation: Different estimators convert the same annotation budget into recovery with different efficiency.
negative_interpretation: If ranks change under another panel, the conclusion remains panel-specific.

supported_claim: The 100% values are comparable anchors but were generated independently of the low-label sampling campaign.
evidence: Frozen matched full-label summary; grey boundary and dashed bridge.
not_supported: The dashed line is not a fitted interpolation and does not imply monotonicity.
positive_interpretation: The anchor provides a common calibration endpoint.
negative_interpretation: Disagreement between 20% and 100% can reflect campaign or estimator variation and must not be overinterpreted.
